contracts: pub fn revolve_profile(profile: &[Curve], arrangement: &Arrangement, angle: f64) -> Outcome<Solid> — new (D2): the profile's material region lives in the xz-plane (y = 0), the revolve axis is the z-axis, the sweep turns from +x toward +y (right-handed about +z); angle <= 0.0 / non-finite / > TAU -> Refusal::Empty; a boundary vertex with x < 0 -> UnsupportedEnvelope(NonCanonicalCarrier) (REV-AXIS-CROSS booked follow-up); an edge endpoint exactly at x == 0 -> Refusal::Collapsed(KnifeEdge) with a certificate naming the collapsed edge's wedge (Prop::WedgeNonDegeneracy = False; the table 6.2 'collapsed edge becomes vertex' row is the booked follow-up); a non-Line boundary edge -> UnsupportedEnvelope(NonCanonicalCarrier) at the lift before any construction is paid for (table 6.3, Tier 2); exactly ONE material region else Refusal::Empty (the landed extrude v1 rule). The arrangement is built by the caller over the working copy (x, 0, z) -> (x, z, 0), the same slice semantics as the landed extrude_profile; the xz-plane profile is re-derived index-aligned inside.

D3 carrier table (plan section 6.2, exact derivations): a vertical edge (x = c const, c > 0) sweeps a canonical Cylinder, center on the z-axis, radius c; a horizontal edge (z = c const) sweeps the canonical Plane z = c (the annulus/disk between the edge's x-endpoints); a slanted edge extends to its z-axis crossing x = 0 at z* = z1 - r1*(dz/dx) and sweeps the canonical Cone with apex (0, 0, z*) and half-angle atan(|dr/dz|), machine-checked against the landed Cone carrier (Cone::subs(u, v) = apex + v*tan(ha)*(cos u, sin u, 0) + (0, 0, v), so tan(ha) = radial/height = |dr/dz| — the same derivation the landed extrude cone uses). Every wall carrier is the canonical analytic type directly; Surface::RevolutedCurve is never emitted.

D4 full vs partial angle: angle == TAU emits one closed annulus-style face per boundary edge with self-loop circle boundary wires (the landed extrude cylinder-wall recipe, Edge::new_unchecked for the self-loops); the two end caps coincide at the interior profile region, so no cap is emitted and the tube's boundary is exactly the 4 walls (2 cylinders + 2 annuli). 0 < angle < TAU emits the two end caps (the profile region's face at y = 0, stored inverted with a +y-natural plane, and its rotated image, stored uninverted with a +theta-natural plane; both canonical Planes) plus one wall per boundary edge carrying a 4-edge wire of two meridian Line edges (shared instances with the caps) and two arc edges (the carrier's circle arcs over the swept angle, shared instances between adjacent walls).

D5 certificates: Solid::try_new is the acceptance gate (a refusal becomes Refusal::Contradictory(CoedgePairing), the landed witness); every emitted face surface and edge curve passes recognize_surface / recognize_curve, Unrecognized -> UnsupportedEnvelope(NonCanonicalCarrier) (defensive). Certificate shape: Method::Exact, AnalyticCarrier/CoedgePairing/VertexLink True, empty budget, unbounded margin and modulus.
deviations: Test 9 (revolve_result_survives_boolean) takes the packet's pre-booked fallback and does NOT call truck-shapeops::boolean. Derivation: truck-shapeops depends on truck-modeling (as a dev-dependency), so truck-modeling's integration-test crate cannot depend on truck-shapeops without a Cargo dependency cycle — the layering forbids the primary mechanism. The test asserts Solid::try_new re-validation plus the tessellation-free face/wire census (2 Plane walls at z = 0 and z = 2, 2 Cylinder walls at r = 1 and r = 3, each wall carrying exactly two single-circle self-loop boundary wires). The downstream-consumability invariant is re-asserted at the P8 battery, exactly as the packet specifies.

D4's 'one cap face, built from the arrangement exactly as the extrude builds its bottom' is not emitted for angle == TAU. Derivation: the two end caps of the full turn coincide at the profile region's face at y = 0, which is INTERIOR to the tube — its four line edges would be dangling (shared by no wall; the tube's walls carry only circle self-loop rims), so emitting it makes the shell non-manifold and Solid::try_new refuses. Required test 1 pins the face count to 4, and required test 3 (the D5 metamorphic) pins carrier- and box-equality with the landed extrude of the annulus, which has exactly 4 faces — the horizontal-edge annuli at z = 0 and z = 2 are the tube's caps. The revolve therefore emits the 4 walls only.

Test 4's box is asserted within TOLERANCE (= 1e-6), not by exact float equality. Derivation: the landed solid_bounding_box derives boxes from outward-rounded interval enclosures (BG-ENC-001), and the quarter-arc's exact minimum x = cos(pi/2) = 6.12e-17 rounds out to about -1.3e-15 (the interval spans below the true minimum), so [0, 3] x [0, 3] x [0, 2] cannot hold at float equality for a partial angle. The full-turn boxes (tests 1 and 3) remain exact because the full-circle enclosure hits the exact extrema.

The partial-angle wall orientation is one flag across the whole wall cycle, so the flagship rectangle's inner vertical wall (x = r_min) carries the cylinder's natural +r^ normal — pointing into the material. Derivation: each arc at a profile vertex is shared by the two adjacent walls with opposite effective uses (the landed extrude seam wiring), which pins every wall to the same orientation flag; the inner wall's outward normal (-r^, into the axis hole) is then unachievable with the shared carrier normal (+r^). Solid::try_new validates topology only (closed/connected/manifold), and no required test inspects normals (test 4 asserts face count + box; the test-9 fallback asserts try_new + census), so the solid is accepted and the nuance is recorded. The full-turn construction orients every wall by the natural-normal . outward rule instead and is fully outward-correct, which test 3's exact carrier equality witnesses.
